report_name: Vishing Campaign 'PREY-0058' Targets Execs for M365 Data Theft

threat_actors.name: PREY-0058
threat_actors.description: A threat cluster conducting a sophisticated data extortion campaign targeting high-level corporate employees. The group uses vishing, AitM phishing, and residential proxies to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts, steal session tokens, and exfiltrate data for extortion.

threat_actors.name: UNC6671
threat_actors.description: A threat actor tracked by Mandiant whose TTPs show a significant overlap with the PREY-0058 campaign.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Voice
attack_patterns.description: The attack begins with a phone call (vishing) to a targeted executive, where the attacker spoofs the company's IT help desk phone number and uses social engineering.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: During the vishing call, the victim is directed to a malicious adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) website.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: The malicious site is an Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) phishing platform that intercepts the entire authentication flow to capture the session cookie.

attack_patterns.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Tokens
attack_patterns.description: The AitM framework captures the resulting session cookie after the user enters their credentials and completes the MFA prompt, which is then used for session replay.

attack_patterns.name: External Proxy
attack_patterns.description: Logins using the stolen session cookie are routed through residential proxy services like NodeMaven to evade detection and make the malicious logins appear to originate from legitimate residential ISPs.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Email Collection
attack_patterns.description: After gaining access with the stolen session token, attackers access and exfiltrate data from Exchange Online.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage Object
attack_patterns.description: Attackers exfiltrate large volumes of data from cloud storage services including SharePoint, OneDrive, and Box.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers use stolen session tokens to gain unauthorized access to victims' Microsoft 365 cloud accounts.

attack_patterns.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
attack_patterns.description: The AitM phishing site proxies the MFA prompt to the victim, tricking them into approving the request on their device, which allows the attackers to capture the session token.

attack_patterns.name: DNS
attack_patterns.description: The use of residential proxies for C2 and access involves DNS lookups to resolve the proxy infrastructure.

tools.name: NodeMaven
tools.description: A residential proxy service used by the attackers to route their malicious logins and evade IP-based detection.

campaigns.name: PREY-0058
campaigns.description: A widespread data theft and extortion campaign targeting corporate executives' Microsoft 365 accounts through a combination of vishing and adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing.

identities.name: Corporate Executives
identities.description: High-level corporate employees, including directors and vice presidents, targeted by the PREY-0058 campaign for their access to sensitive data.

infrastructure.name: AitM Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A malicious adversary-in-the-middle phishing platform used to intercept user credentials and session tokens for Microsoft 365.

infrastructure.name: Residential Proxy Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A network of residential proxies used to mask the origin of malicious logins and bypass geofencing policies.

infrastructure.name: Phishing Lure Domains
infrastructure.description: Malicious domains crafted to look legitimate, often using patterns like <victim organization>.<lure domain> (e.g., acme-corp.mfaregister.com), to host the AitM phishing page.

indicators.name: PREY-0058 Phishing Lure Domains
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: PREY-0058 Phishing Lure Domain DNS Query
id: 2f8b1c9a-7d3e-4f1a-9b8c-6d5e4f3a2b1c
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to domains known to be used in the PREY-0058 vishing and data extortion campaign.
references:
  - https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/prey-0058-vishing-campaign-targets-microsoft-365/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-07
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.initial_access
level: high
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'mfaregister.com'
      - 'setpasskey.com'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects DNS queries for domains associated with the PREY-0058 AitM phishing infrastructure.

indicators.name: Anomalous Microsoft 365 File Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Microsoft 365 File Access
id: 5e4d3c2b-1a9f-4e8d-7c6b-5a4b3c2d1e9f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects file access events in Microsoft 365 (SharePoint, OneDrive). This activity itself is often benign, but should be correlated with other signals like suspicious sign-ins (e.g., from non-corporate or residential proxy ASNs) or impossible travel alerts. A high volume of these events from a single session may indicate data exfiltration as seen in the PREY-0058 campaign.
references:
  - https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/prey-0058-vishing-campaign-targets-microsoft-365/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-07
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.collection
level: medium
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.sharepoint
detection:
  selection:
    Operation:
      - FileDownloaded
      - FileAccessed
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects file access events in Microsoft 365. A high volume of these events from a single session, especially when correlated with a suspicious sign-in, may indicate data exfiltration.
